result.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
result.comment: 48 pages, 14 figures, 26 tables. Companion paper to "AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics" (Sharpe et al., 2026)
result.summary: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ISLA，一种面向稳态、边界驱动 PDE 的 slice-attention transformer：不使用绝对坐标，位置仅以到可学习 slice anchor 的距离与相对角进入计算，长度以边界导出的单位度量，边界求和实现为求积，内部点通过树加速核查询边界，从而获得刚体运动/反射等变性、单位不变性与网格细化一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「anchor 相对几何 + 边界即 token 的查询」设计可能为 LVR 中如何在内部状态保几何与任务必要信息、以及如何筛选视觉证据提供可核查的架构线索，但研究对象是物理场回归而非 VLM 推理，迁移性需自行判断。
